claim: At initialization, the output functions of a neural network converge in law to i.i.d. centered Gaussian processes in the infinite-width limit.
stance_target: N5: infinite-width networks ARE Gaussian processes, so finite ensembles approximate a GP posterior
scope_conditions: Networks of arbitrary depth L with Lipschitz nonlinearity, infinite-width limit n1,...,nL-1 -> infinity
quoted_support: As observed in (16; 4; 7; 13; 6), the output functions fθ,i for i = 1, ..., nL tend to iid Gaussian processes in the infinite-width limit (a proof in our setup is given in the appendix).

claim: In the infinite-width limit, the Neural Tangent Kernel converges in probability to a deterministic limiting kernel that stays constant during training, making gradient descent equivalent to kernel gradient descent in a fixed RKHS.
stance_target: N5: infinite-width networks behave as fixed, well-behaved kernel machines rather than accumulating training-induced jaggedness
quoted_support: The first key result of our paper (proven in the appendix) is the following: in the same limit, the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) converges in probability to an explicit deterministic limit.

claim: Wider networks produce an empirical NTK with less variance and greater smoothness than narrower networks, and this smoothness advantage grows as training proceeds.
stance_target: N5 adversarial reading: ensemble posterior-mean jaggedness is a finite-width/under-training artifact, not an intrinsic surrogate-class property
scope_conditions: Depth-4 network, widths n=500 vs n=10000, least-squares regression on random N(0,1) inputs, 200 gradient-descent steps
quoted_support: For the wider network, the NTK shows less variance and is smoother. It is interesting to note that the expectation of the NTK is very close for both networks widths.

claim: After training, the NTK of a narrower network 'inflates' more than that of a wider network, i.e. instability/variance under training is width-dependent and shrinks as width grows.
stance_target: N5 adversarial reading: width/under-training artifact explanation for jagged posterior means
scope_conditions: Depth-4 network, widths n=500 vs n=10000
quoted_support: After 200 steps of training, we observe that the NTK tends to ‘inflate.’ As expected, this effect is much less apparent for the wider network (n = 10000) where the NTK stays almost fixed, than for the smaller network (n = 500).

claim: Jacot et al. never discuss Bayesian ensembles, posterior distributions from trained finite ensembles, acquisition functions, surrogate models, or model-based optimization -- the paper is purely about supervised training dynamics.
stance_target: N5/N6: scope boundary of the NTK paper relative to offline-MBO surrogate/ensemble claims
